title: Valmont Legacy Redesign
description: Five legacy applications modernised into one unified enterprise web experience.

hero.headline: Five legacy applications. One unified enterprise experience.

paragraphs: Valmont Industries — a global leader in infrastructure and agricultural irrigation systems — was running critical internal operations on a suite of aging desktop applications. Built on outdated UI frameworks, they were difficult to use, inconsistent in experience, and costly to maintain.

As the embedded Product Designer, I was responsible for researching the legacy systems, understanding how field teams and internal staff actually used them, and translating those workflows into a cohesive, modern enterprise web experience.
overview.quote: Five applications. Five different eras of UI. One mission — bring them all into a single, unified, modern experience that people actually want to use.

process.heading: Research-first. Workflow-faithful. Delivered across seven phases.
process.description: Before touching a single frame in Figma, I spent considerable time understanding how each legacy application functioned — not just technically, but behaviourally. The key principle: fidelity to original workflows. Not reinventing processes — elevating them.

phases.title: Research
phases.description: Studied legacy desktop apps, documented existing user flows, identified pain points and missing UX patterns.

phases.title: Information Architecture
phases.description: Restructured navigation, content hierarchy, and data groupings to match real user mental models.

phases.title: Wireframing
phases.description: Low-fidelity wireframes to validate layout decisions and flow logic before committing to visual design.

phases.title: Visual Design
phases.description: High-fidelity UI built on Valmont brand guidelines — clean, neutral, data-forward with Valley blue.

phases.title: Design System
phases.description: Shared component library and decision system used across all five applications for full consistency.

phases.title: Dev Handoff
phases.description: Structured, developer-friendly Figma files with annotations and spacing specs for seamless implementation.

phases.title: Prototyping
phases.description: Interactive prototypes for stakeholder reviews and usability walkthroughs — testing before building.

applications.heading: Five applications transformed — before and after.
applications.description: Each application presented unique challenges — from Windows-era desktop UIs to raw data tables with no visual hierarchy. The approach remained consistent: research deeply, design from the user's perspective, deliver clean Figma files.

apps.name: AG Portal
apps.subtitle: Central launchpad for Valmont's internal applications
apps.insight: The portal redesign set the tone for the entire suite — establishing the Valley brand header, navigation patterns, and component language used across all five applications.

apps.name: SPIN II
apps.subtitle: Production planning tool — scheduling data and planner management

apps.name: Security App
apps.subtitle: User access, roles, and permissions management across Valmont's systems
apps.insight: One of the most complex redesigns — managing nested permission structures required careful IA to keep all controls accessible without overwhelming administrators.

apps.name: SOS — Schedule of Supply
apps.subtitle: Weekly supply scheduling across production sites

outcome.quote: Across three years of embedded design work, five disconnected, aging desktop applications became a cohesive, modern enterprise web experience — built on a shared design system and ready for development handoff.

deliverables.title: Design System
deliverables.description: Shared component library following Valmont brand guidelines — used across all 5 apps.

deliverables.title: 50+ Screens
deliverables.description: Wireframes, high-fidelity UI, and interactive prototypes for every flow and state.

deliverables.title: Dev-Ready Files
deliverables.description: Structured, annotated Figma files for seamless engineering handoff.

deliverables.title: Unified UX
deliverables.description: Consistent navigation, patterns, and visual language across all 5 applications.
